data_section_full_text:
Financial Analysis Made Easy”(FAME) database supplied


by Bureau Van Dijk . This database provides accounting data on over 100,000 private British


companies for fiscal years ending after January 1989. The database is compiled from records filed at


the Companies House in Cardiff, London and Edinburgh, and supplemented with information taken from


the London and Edinburgh Gazettes. The database is updated monthly and the particular data for this


study are obtained from the March 2000 and earlier versions of the database. Since data availability is


limited in initial years, we restrict our sample period to the five-year period 1994-98. <sup>10</sup>


Apart from the advantage of providing financial information on private companies, this database


has little survivorship bias since the coverage starts as soon as a firm files its annual accounts with the


Companies House and stops as soon as the firm stops functioning as a separate unit. No back data are


added as in COMPUSTAT. The database includes only companies that either have annual turnover in


excess of £750,000 or pre-tax profits greater than £45,000 or shareholders’ funds greater than


£750,000. Further, we exclude firms with less than £1 million in total assets. Thus, very small


companies are not in our sample. Finally, banks, insurance and other financial institutions are excluded


from this database as their reports do not fit the general format used by other companies.


Changes in organization type (i.e., conversion from private to listed or listed to private) were


identified by comparing the company type code across various years.  We excluded any firm-year in


which a firm changed its organizational type. We also excluded all firm-years in which the fiscal year


was not exactly twelve months. In addition, we screened out observations for which book value of total


assets changed by over 30% from the prior year. These are likely to be firm-years in which a major


10 Fiscal years are converted into calendar years using the same approach as COMPUSTAT. That is, fiscal years
ending before May 31 <sup>st</sup> are treated as belonging to the previous calendar year, while those ending on or after June 1 <sup>st</sup>
are classified as belonging to the same calendar year as the year in which the financial statements are prepared.


22

acquisition, restructuring or divestment occurred. <sup>11</sup> Further, we excluded firm-years in which accounting


numbers were inconsistent (e.g., revenues, expenses and profits were inconsistent) or irreconcilable


across the different monthly versions of FAME. We lose less than 0.5% of the observations because of


this last criterion. Including these firms in the sample has no material impact on our results. Our final


sample consists of a yearly median of 15,255 (mean of 15,484) private firm observations.
